interest: Return of war dead from Japan, including six airmen recovered by the Soviets.
overview: This file consists of U.S. State Department correspondence, diplomatic despatches, military telegrams, and internal transfer/charge slips spanning August 1947 to July 1949 under decimal file 894.123311, which concerns cemeteries and the disposal and maintenance of graves of U.S. and Allied soldiers, sailors, and civilians in occupied Japan. Key matters documented include diplomatic negotiations conducted through the American Embassy at The Hague with the Netherlands Foreign Ministry and the Netherlands East Indies Government regarding permission to repatriate cremated Allied remains from Japanese mass graves to the United States; a Far East Command cable reporting the Soviet handover of six casketed American airmen recovered from Cape Lopatka, Kamchatka; a request by the father of Staff Sergeant Solomon H. Groner under Public Law 368 to transfer his son's remains from Yokohama Cemetery No. 1 to Jerusalem, Palestine for private burial; an inquiry from New Zealand regarding the burial location of USMC Captain Edward Glenn Walker, killed at Tarawa; and a series of Division of Communications and Records transfer slips documenting the reclassification of correspondence from Jimmy Waldegg concerning the transport of his father's urn from Tokyo to Bogotá, Colombia, from the Japan file to Colombian decimal file 394.633.
